title: Growing up with Tillman and the first band
summary: Russ's first band was Tillman's, with boyhood friends from Sixteenth Ward; they fooled with cheap flutes and formed a band together.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: What was the first band you stayed with?
That's right. He and I raised up together. Are you from uptown? I'm from Sixteen Ward. Is that Carrollton?
Tillman's from up there. That's very recent. He's four years old anymore.
Well, when you were a kid, did you fool around with any little homemade instruments or anything like that, like Tillman did?
He fooled. Tillman played fool with the clarinet.
Oh, I thought he fooled around with a tin flute and stuff like that.
No. Oh, we were. Yeah, we were. We were fooling around with a flute, you know. Yeah? The bomb fifteen cents flute at the dragon stone.
Yeah, that was our philosophy, you know. And, uh, well, Tillman and I raised up together. His brother-in-law, you got Alan Gorda in there?
We all started out together. Mm-hmm. We all raised up together.

Tillman, call him Hunter, we can call him Hunter, his name is Alan Gorda. Mm-hmm. Willie Newton, Joe Mudhouse, Old Man Nighy, well Tillman's brother, he started playing, but he didn't last long, he didn't stay too long. That was the band that was the first band we started up.
